Settings.Title: Settings
Settings.Worklist.Enabled: Offer the worklist when entering patient details
Settings.Worklist.CallingAeOverride: Calling AE Title for the worklist
Settings.Worklist.CallingAeOverride.Capt: Leave empty to use this workstation’s own AE Title, which is what most sites want. Set it only when the worklist server expects a different name from the archive.
Settings.Worklist.Modality.Caption: Leave empty to list every modality, which is usually right for a department converting documents. Enter a value such as OT to narrow it.
Settings.Worklist.Range.AnyDate: Any date (can be slow on a busy worklist)
Settings.Worklist.ScheduledStation.Capti: Leave blank to match every station, which is usually right: the document is filed from a desk, not from the scheduled device.
Settings.Worklist.ExplicitDates.Caption: These two dates are used only when the interval above is set to an explicit range. Either may be left empty, in which case today is used for that end.
Settings.Worklist.MaximumResults.Caption: A guard against a mistyped search returning an entire schedule. The list says so when it has been cut short.
Settings.Worklist.AcceptAnyCertificate.C: Convenient on a closed network with a self signed certificate, and a hole anywhere else: it stops the worklist server being authenticated at all.
Worklist.Title: Modality Worklist
Worklist.Subtitle: Choose the scheduled procedure this document belongs to. The patient details are taken from it, so nothing has to be typed.
Worklist.Truncated: More results were available than can be shown; narrow the search.
Worklist.Shortened: shortened to fit what DICOM allows
Worklist.Column.Name: Name
Settings.OrganizationUidRoot.ToolTip: Registered to the publisher of this software and fixed in it. It is shown partly masked and cannot be edited.
Settings.OrganizationUidRoot.Caption: Registered with Medical Connections Ltd and issued to the author of this software, so it is fixed and cannot be changed here. Choose it above when your PACS prefers identifiers under a registered arc; the UUID option is the default and is unique by construction.
Settings.StudyGrouping.Separate: Each file in its own study
Settings.StudyGrouping.ByPatient: Files for the same patient share one study
Settings.StudyGrouping.Caption: Grouping puts every file converted for the same Patient ID into one study, each file still in its own series, so a viewer shows them together but separately. The association lasts until the patient changes or the application is closed, and is never saved, so a later examination cannot join an old study by accident. A Study Instance UID typed on the form always wins.
Settings.ImageModality.Caption: Written to Modality (0008,0060) on converted images. OT (Other) is accepted everywhere. XC is the defined term for external camera photography. This is kept separate from the document modality because DOC would be wrong on a photograph.
Settings.RenderPdfPagesAsImages: Also send each page of a PDF as an image
Settings.RenderPdfPagesAsImages.Caption: Many PACS viewers will only open a study that contains an image, and an encapsulated PDF is not one. With this on, every page is also sent as a Secondary Capture image in its own series, so the viewer opens and the report is readable. Turn it off if your viewer already displays encapsulated documents; it roughly doubles what is stored and sent.
ConversionType.WSD: Workstation (created on a workstation or console)
ConversionType.SD: Scanned Document (a paper document scanned into DICOM)
ConversionType.DV: Digitized Video (captured from a video feed)
ConversionType.DI: Digital Interface (transferred via a digital interface)
ConversionType.DF: Digitized Film (an analog film X-ray or similar scanned via a digitizer)
ConversionType.SYN: Synthetic Image (an image created algorithmically or rendered from data)
Settings.BurnedInAnnotation: Document contains identifying text (Burned In Annotation)
Settings.AutoDelete: Delete the generated DICOM file after a successful transmission
Settings.AlwaysSaveLocally: Always keep a copy of the generated DICOM file
Settings.EnableFolderMonitoring: Monitor a folder for new PDF documents
Settings.ShowAdvancedFields: Show advanced DICOM fields on the main window

About.Offline: This application works entirely offline. The only network activity is the DICOM transmission to the configured destinations.
Settings.Import.Intro: Where documents arrive from another system with the patient details already in the file name, those details can be read instead of retyped. Nothing is sent without confirmation: the file name fills the form, and the operator still sees what is about to go and against whom.
Settings.Import.Enabled: Read the patient details from the file name
Settings.Import.Enabled.Caption: Applies to documents picked up from the monitored folder, which is configured on the Folders page. A file the operator opens by hand is never interpreted or moved.
Settings.Import.Patterns.Caption: Write the layout the way the names look, for example {PatientId}_{Name}_{AccessionNumber}. Available fields: {PatientId} {Name} {FamilyName} {GivenName} {AccessionNumber} {DateOfBirth} {StudyDescription}, and {*} for a part to ignore. Everything outside the braces must appear exactly as written. List as many layouts as you need; the one that reads the most fields is used, so the order does not matter. A line starting with regex: is a regular expression with named groups. Leave the extension out.
Settings.Import.DateFormats: Date of birth formats, one per line
Settings.Import.DateFormats.Caption: Leave empty to accept yyyyMMdd, yyyy-MM-dd, ddMMyyyy, dd-MM-yyyy and dd.MM.yyyy. A format containing a slash can never match, because a file name cannot contain one. A date that matches no format is left empty rather than guessed at, and the reason is written to the log.
Settings.Import.PadPatientId: Pad the patient number to this many digits
Settings.Import.PadPatientId.Caption: Sending systems often drop the leading zeros, writing 77 where your records hold 0000000077. Those are different patients as far as an archive is concerned. Set this to the width your archive stores, or 0 to use the number exactly as the file name has it. Only a number is padded: an identifier containing letters is left alone, and a longer one is never shortened.
Settings.Import.DefaultSex.Caption: File names almost never carry the sex. O means other, M and F are the obvious ones, and an empty box records the field as empty, which is also correct. The operator can change it on the form before sending.
Settings.Import.UseFileDate: Use the file's date as the study date
Settings.Import.UseFileDate.Caption: The date and time the file was created, which is normally when the other system issued the document. The date this application created the DICOM object is recorded separately, so both are kept. Switch this off to use the moment of conversion for both.
Settings.Import.SplitNames: Split a run-together name such as JohnDoe
Settings.Import.SplitNames.Caption: Reads JohnDoe as John Doe. This is a guess, and it is wrong for a surname such as McDonald or DaSilva, so it is off unless you know the sending software writes names this way. With it off, JohnDoe becomes the surname on its own. Try a real name in the box below before relying on it.
Settings.Import.After: Once a document has been dealt with
Settings.Import.After.Leave: Leave it alone (it will be offered again)
Settings.Import.After.Caption: The original must stop looking like new work, or the same document is offered every time. Nothing is ever deleted and nothing is ever overwritten: if a file of the same name is already there, a number is added to the new one.
Settings.Import.ImportedSubfolder: Subfolder for documents that were sent
Settings.Import.FailedSubfolder: Subfolder for documents that were not
Settings.Import.FailedSubfolder.Caption: A document that failed, or whose name matched no layout, always goes here, whatever the setting above says. It needs somebody to look at it, which cannot happen if it stays in the watched folder.
Settings.Import.RenameSuffix.Caption: Added after the extension, so report.pdf becomes report.pdf.imported and no longer looks like a PDF.
Settings.Import.Test.Caption: Type a real file name and see exactly what would be read from it. This uses the settings as they are above, so there is no need to save first. Nothing is converted and nothing is sent; the file does not even have to exist.
Settings.Import.Test.Empty: Type a file name above, then press Read it.
Settings.Lock.LockedCaption.Worklist: The worklist can be searched without a password. Changing which servers it talks to needs one, so a connection that works is not altered by accident. The same password opens the Destinations page.
Settings.Lock.LockedCaption.Destinations: Documents can be sent without a password. Changing where they are sent needs one: a mistyped address or AE Title puts a patient's report in the wrong archive. The same password opens the Worklist page.
Settings.Lock.Unprotected: No password has been set in this build, so these settings are open to anyone who opens this dialog. Run "pdftodicom settings-password" and rebuild to set one.
Settings.Worklist.Name: Name shown to the operator
Settings.Worklist.Name.Caption: What this worklist is called when the operator chooses between them, for example "Radiology" or "Cardiology". Say what the worklist holds rather than where it lives.
Worklist.NoServers: No worklist server is enabled. Add one on the Worklist page in Settings.
Worklist.PatientIdHint: Enter a patient number to fetch that patient. A single match is selected for you; where there are several, pick the right one from the list. Leave both boxes empty for the whole scheduled list.
